text:
sam_support: FYI — Acme reported an unexpected ~65k token bump on last night's invoice. Their app logs show no corresponding spike. Can we triage?

maria_sre: ugh, okay. which deployment? private VPC or onprem?

sam_support: private deployment in eu-west-1, agent v1.14.2 running on customer-host-03. They attached audit logs showing continuous small requests.

alex_eng: I pulled the customer's agent logs. seeing a tight window where the agent flushed a long backlog after an NTP step. sample: 
```
2025-11-01T03:01:12Z INFO buffer: flush triggered (offline buffer size=65k tokens)
2025-11-01T03:01:12Z WARN time: ntp step detected +128s, adjusting local clock
2025-11-01T03:01:13Z INFO meter_client: send batch seq_start=987650 seq_end=987715 items=66
2025-11-01T03:01:15Z ERROR meter_client: ack mismatch: server accepted seq 987650-987715, but audit shows same events were already delivered at 2025-11-01T01:52:xx
```

metering-bot: me:ingest:batch_written batch_id=20251101-030112 seq=[987650..987715] items=66

maria_sre: so the agent buffered offline (expected) and then an NTP step made timestamps jump forward which caused the agent to treat previously-seen events as new when it flushed?

alex_eng: short version: offline buffering + clock step + non-monotonic seq acceptance on the collector = duplicated token accounting. The audit log on the customer side only has the original events (so audit vs meter diverge).

sam_support: do we have a quick repro? customer expects root cause before we offer a credit.

alex_eng: repro in our internal lab:
1) start agent v1.14.2, let it collect a small backlog while offline.
2) simulate system clock step forward (`sudo date -s "+130 seconds"`)
3) bring network back up -> agent flushes buffer in one batch; collector treats batch timestamps as new and increments usage ledger.

Example agent sequence (local):
```
# before network restored
queued_events = 217
# after ntp step and restore
flush -> batch seq_start=2001 seq_end=2217
collector ledger adds tokens for 217 events again (no dedupe)
```

maria_sre: thanks — looks like collector needs monotonic-seq enforcement or stronger idempotency on ingestion. We also should harden agent so flushed batches carry a monotonic client-side monotonic ID that survives clock jumps.

alex_eng: agree. immediate mitigation options:
- update collector to ignore batches with seq ranges that overlap previously-seen seq IDs for that customer (safe but needs careful storage)
- short-term: add `--force-monotonic-seq` flag to agents to prefix batches with a persistently-incrementing UUID; collector can dedupe on that

metering-bot: action_required ticket created: MTR-5912 "private-agent flush duplication on clock step" assigned -> infra-metering (priority: high)

ingrid_csm: Customer wants a remediation plan + timeline. Can we promise a temporary credit while we fix?

maria_sre: yes, recommend offering a one-off invoice adjustment for the window in question. ops/legal ok'd manual credits for confirmed ingestion duplication.

sam_support: sent customer a note: "we identified a duplication path from agent clock jumps during offline flush; we will credit the excess and roll a fix next week." They asked for technical summary — included the log snippet.

alex_eng: I'll open a PR tomorrow to add `monotonic_batch_id` to the agent and collector dedupe logic. POC timeline: 48h. Full rollout after tests: 2 weeks.

maria_sre: also circling back to monitoring: add a detector for large overnight flush sizes + NTP events per host so we can auto-flag these before invoices process.

ingrid_csm: I'll schedule a 30m customer call for tomorrow to walk them through the plan. Notifying them of the credit now reduces churn risk. :thumbsup:

sam_support: thanks all — update the ticket with the PR link and keep me posted. Closing loop with customer after fix deployed.

metering-bot: ticket MTR-5912 status updated -> in_progress (assignee: alex_eng)
